records.note: Compound structural claim. The workforce comparative ('vastly more primary care doctors than there will ever be psychiatrists') describes a state already true at the statement date and names no series or threshold; 'ever' is not a deadline. The prescribing clause ('tools at their disposal, which are overwhelmingly not psychotherapy') has no countable set, named series or threshold. Nothing resolvable can be written.

Publication of the author's own tool (TDscreen.ai, built with Videra Health and iRxReminder, both disclosed affiliations) is a publication of the forecaster's own organizations. 'Soon' is also not a deadline.

Utility claim about the author's own product (TDscreen.ai; Videra Health and iRxReminder are disclosed affiliations). No third party decides whether the tool 'will help screen'. 'Vastly greater simplicity' is also a comparative without a benchmark, and the tool is described as existing now.

'More are coming to market soon' is a quantifier with no countable set: no device, developer, regulator or indication is named. 'Soon' is not a deadline. 'Vastly broader use' of TMS is a comparative without a benchmark or series.

A TMS manufacturer supplying a sham coil to investigators on request is not a regulatory, trial, company or market, payer or practice-adoption outcome. The manufacturer is also unnamed, so no entity can be written.

Doubt about a present scientific hypothesis (whether 30 percent output iTBS is itself active). No future state is asserted; no replication trial, sponsor or readout is named, so any call about what a better-controlled replication would show is only implied.

'Should be replicated', reinforced by 'I'm writing this article to suggest somebody do' it, is a recommendation with no predictive reading. 'Potentially a big-deal finding' evaluates the Koparal et al. result and names no trial, endpoint or date.
The author's own live event (RAMHT, disclosed affiliation as organizer) on 18 May 2025 in Los Angeles. Own-organization event; also outside the five areas.

'The time for scams is over' is a slogan closing a think piece. No payer, vendor, policy, series or threshold is named, and the value-based care vendor it refers to is a satirical sketch. Nothing resolvable can be written.

'TMS researchers will soon find a way to modulate it' names no trial, program, endpoint or sponsor; 'find a way to modulate' has no observable criterion, and 'soon' is not a deadline. The named colleagues are credited, not forecast about.

Descriptive setup ('Today's article focuses on two new lines of evidence that suggest ...'). 'May be promising' evaluates existing evidence and asserts no future state; no trial, clearance, guideline or payer decision is named.

Evident irony: 'with luck', the 'absurd and degrading' prior-authorization process 'we love today', and 'if it feels closer than ever!'. The 20-year horizon is hyperbole, not a sincere date. The underlying sincere point (payer coverage of TMS for schizophrenia will lag the evidence) names no payer decision or date that could be written without treating the ironic figure as sincere.
The newsletter's own publication schedule (part III 'tomorrow'). Own-organization action; also outside the five areas.
'Are going to bear tremendous fruit' is a slogan: no device, trial, clearance, series or threshold. Section headline; the sub-claims are logged separately (owen-1671 to owen-1674).

'Rapidly becoming possible' across nine indications names no trial, clearance, guideline or series; 'possible' has no observable criterion and 'rapidly' is not a deadline. Compound claim with nothing resolvable.

'More are coming for depression, PTSD, and other disorders' is a quantifier with no countable set: no device, developer, regulator or clearance pathway is named, and 'come to market' is not tied to any decision. 'Coming' is not a deadline. A device_authorization entry would need the regulator, device class and indication boundary invented.

'Seems extremely promising' for waking coma patients and for depression or PTSD names no trial, sponsor, endpoint or clearance; the author states it is research-stage only ('yet' is not a deadline). Two indications in one hedge, nothing resolvable.
'The future is both now, and more is coming!' is a slogan; 'more' has no countable set and 'is coming' is not a deadline.
Own newsletter plan (further installments of the McAndrews conversation). Own-organization action; also outside the five areas.
Own newsletter plan (a next chat with Kyle McAndrews). Own-organization action; also outside the five areas.

'I hope ... will make a real difference' marks aspiration, and even read as a call, 'a real difference' has no benchmark, series or threshold; no device, trial or decision is named for Parkinson's disease. Ampa Health (a disclosed trial-site affiliation) appears only in context.
Own event (RAMHT '25; the author is the organizer): Ampa Health's appearance at the author's own event is arranged by the organizer. Own-organization action; also outside the five areas.

Descriptive status ('isn't cleared for the treatment of PD yet, no TMS treatment is') plus a requirement ('we will need design thinking'). No clearance, filing or date is asserted; 'yet' alone does not forecast a clearance. Ampa is a disclosed trial-site affiliation.
LinkedIn post performance is not one of the five areas. Also a generic conditional with no benchmark for 'do well'.

Own event (RAMHT '25 LA, 18 May 2025). Own-organization action; also outside the five areas.

event.asset: Early-TMS randomized trial (rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI as early treatment of depression in pregnancy; Becker-Sadzio et al. protocol, 2025)
event.title: Early-TMS trial reports its rTMS-versus-SSRI comparison in pregnant women with depression
event.proposition: The Early-TMS randomized trial reports its primary comparison of rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI treatment in pregnant women with depression (either direction).
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first public report of the Early-TMS trial's primary outcome result: the peer-reviewed primary results publication, or the investigators' topline release or a results posting in the trial registry named in the Becker-Sadzio et al. 2025 protocol, whichever is first. The result may favour either arm or neither; the event is about a primary result being reported. The protocol publication, a recruitment update, an interim safety report or a conference abstract without the primary outcome estimate does not count. Resolution source: the peer-reviewed Early-TMS primary results publication (PubMed), with the trial registry entry named in the protocol as the secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Early-TMS primary results publication (PubMed); trial registry entry named in the Becker-Sadzio et al. 2025 protocol as secondary source

readings: 'One more RCT coming this year' and 'soon, thanks to the Early-TMS trial, we will have a direct comparison' are read together: the claim is that the Early-TMS trial reports its rTMS/iTBS-versus-SSRI comparison in 2025. A coder who reads 'coming this year' as the trial being conducted, not reported, in 2025 would code a different deadline or reject.
The claim is about timing, so the event resolves on the first public report of the primary outcome in either direction, not on which arm wins (the author withholds his pick; see owen-1685).

The trial is identified only by the author's words: the Early-TMS trial, Becker-Sadzio et al. protocol published February 2025, rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI in pregnant women with depression. No registry number is given, so none is written.

records.phrase: we have one more RCT coming this year ... we will have a direct comparison
records.stage_note: At the statement date the Early-TMS protocol had been published (Becker-Sadzio et al., February 2025) and, per the author, the trial 'hasn't been done yet'. No base-rate class covers the timing of a trial readout; abstain.
records.note: Third-party trial: the author has no disclosed role in Early-TMS or its investigators (Acacia Clinics and Ampa are trial sites for other studies), so affiliated is false. 'This year' = 31 December 2025 (anchor). Bin A on 'will' ('we will have a direct comparison'; 'coming' is also an A phrase). Not a report: no source is cited for the timing, and the author states his own expectation from the published protocol. The conduct-versus-readout reading is logged in the event readings. The duplicate capture of the second sentence is owen-1687.

'I hope will meaningfully answer more of the most important questions' marks aspiration, and even read as a call, 'meaningfully answer' has no endpoint, threshold or observable criterion. The readout-timing claim on the same trial is coded at owen-1683.

'I know which I'd be betting on' withholds the pick; the direction (iTBS/rTMS over SSRI) is inferred by the finder from the post's safety thesis and is not stated in the quote or its immediate context. Writing the proposition would invent it. The author also declines to forecast ('we don't have to rely on a gut check or hunches'). The trial's readout timing is coded at owen-1683.

'The science will absolutely LAP the payment models' has no payer, policy, coverage decision, series or threshold; 'lap' cannot be resolved. The condition ('if we don't raise all our voices') is not an observable event. No deadline words.

The same sentence ('And soon, thanks to the Early-TMS trial, we will have a direct comparison') in the same post is already captured inside owen-1683, which stands as the first row. On its own, 'soon' is not a deadline.
Own event (the fourth RAMHT; the author is the organizer). 'Most exciting lineup to date' is also a subjective comparative. Outside the five areas.
Own event date and venue (RAMHT, 18 May 2025, Los Angeles). Own-organization action; also outside the five areas.
Speaker lineup of the author's own event (RAMHT). Whether the listed speakers appear is arranged by the organizer; own-organization event, also outside the five areas.
Own event (RAMHT). 'The most exciting RAMHT event to date' is also a subjective comparative with no benchmark.
Sincere plug for the author's own event (RAMHT, 18 May 2025, Skyline Loft) inside a satirical post. Own-organization event; also outside the five areas.
'Likely to be able to treat other conditions' names no condition, trial, endpoint, clearance or date; 'other conditions' has no countable set.

'Insurance ... will rarely approve treatments in broader populations than the FDA' is a generalization about payer behaviour with no payer, policy, treatment, series or threshold; 'rarely' is not a countable criterion. It describes a standing pattern.

'I'm here to encourage my colleagues at all health plans to update their coverage policy promptly' is advice with no predictive reading. 'Opens them up to tremendous liability' describes present exposure and names no suit, court or date; the lawsuit expectation is coded at owen-1696.

'It is a lawsuit waiting to happen' takes its defendant from context (Cigna/Evernorth's adolescent TMS policy) but names no plaintiff, court, jurisdiction or date, and a lawsuit filing is not one of the eight template outcomes (court_outcome resolves on a verdict, ruling, dismissal or settlement, none of which is claimed). 'Waiting to happen' is neither a lexicon phrase nor an anchor, and the idiom also reads as a description of present risk. Same reading as 'a board complaint waiting to happen' in an earlier packet. The rhetorical question ('do you really want to be in the position ...') is not a claim.
